requirements.title: SS, SP, and S temporarily set the connection sign mode
requirements.definition: SS, SP, and S temporarily change the connection sign mode to SUPPRESS, PLUS, and PROCESSOR_DEFINED respectively.

pending.S-sets-processor-defined: Source-control: S sets the sign mode to PROCESSOR_DEFINED. The optional-plus output latitude of that mode is not asserted here; S13.8.4-002 owns the processor option.
pending.sign-mode-persists-within-statement: WRITE(buf,'(SP,I2,I2)') 7,8; expect exactly '+7+8', showing the changed mode persists for later eligible descriptors in the statement.

requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans use independent literal expected strings or scalar sentinels. Negative plans change one property from a conforming control and attribute the violation to this unit only.

S13.8.4-001 control edit descriptor runtime fixtures: ss_suppresses_optional_plus uses write(buf,'(SS,I2)') 7 and expects ' 7': SS selects SUPPRESS sign mode, so I2 for positive 7 has a leading blank rather than an optional plus. sp_prints_optional_plus uses write(buf,'(SP,I2)') 7 and expects '+7': SP selects PLUS sign mode, so the optional sign position in I2 is a plus before 7.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Pending output plans use internal WRITE to a CHARACTER variable and name exact expected characters including blanks when the unit is internally testable. Unnumbered prose restrictions are not promoted to numbered-constraint diagnostics. Where the source makes a behavior processor dependent, or where a rule requires external stream/direct/sequential files or unregistered defined I/O, the pending plan is explicitly source-control or unassertable rather than a fixture oracle. PROCESSOR_DEFINED sign mode is processor latitude; plus and blank choices are both permitted. The S descriptor facet records only the mandatory mode-setting effect; output latitude is accounted under p2.processor-defined-option.

S13.8.4-001 control edit descriptor fixture boundaries: Only the listed executable facets are represented. Every character-output case pre-fills the internal file variable or array with '#', asserts LEN where a character scalar is observed, and compares the whole field or assembled record with an equal-length literal so blank padding cannot hide a short oracle. The fixtures do not assert processor-defined sign or leading-zero modes, nondefault-character skipped positions, external sequential/stream/direct file positioning, diagnostics, or G0 processor-selected parameters. Mutation plans are generated with each parent source: wrong oracle, changed input value, control-descriptor removal where portable, and descriptor substitutions for T3/T4, TL2/TR2, SP/SS, DC/DP, and BN/BZ.

requirements.title: Sign mode controls optional plus characters for PLUS, SUPPRESS, and PROCESSOR_DEFINED
requirements.definition: PLUS requires plus signs in optional plus positions and SUPPRESS prohibits them; PROCESSOR_DEFINED permits the processor either to produce or omit a plus sign subject to numeric editing rules.

pending.processor-defined-plus-latitude: Permission/source-control: WRITE(buf,'(S,I2)') 7 may produce either '+7' or ' 7' subject to 13.7.2(5); both choices are permitted and a fixture must not require one spelling.

requirements.title: Sign edit descriptors affect only selected numeric output editing and no input editing
requirements.definition: SS, SP, and S affect only I, F, E, EN, ES, EX, D, and G editing during output and have no effect during input.

pending.sign-does-not-affect-character-output: WRITE(buf,'(SP,A1,I2)') 'x',7; expect exactly 'x+7', with A output unchanged by sign mode.
pending.sign-no-effect-input: READ('+7','(SS,I2)') into an integer should produce 7 if the plus sign is otherwise valid; sign descriptors do not change input semantics.
